key_insight: Weakening stratification drives the flow from buoyancy-dominated turbulence to Kelvin–Helmholtz-active mixing and then toward nearly isotropic turbulence, while intermediate stratification produces strong vertically sheared horizontal flows and steeper perpendicular spectra.
engineering_relevance: The results help predict when shear-driven stratified flows will mix efficiently, develop intermittent bursts, or reorganize into anisotropic structures relevant to geophysical, atmospheric, and industrial mixing systems.
method: Direct numerical simulations of stably stratified Kolmogorov-forced shear flow
Parameter sweep over a broad range of Froude numbers to isolate stratification regimes
Spectral transfer, intermittency, and mixing diagnostics used to characterize energy pathways and flow structure
evidence_signal: The abstract reports regime-dependent DNS results showing predominantly forward energy transfer, negative large-scale perpendicular flux from anisotropic redistribution, enhanced kurtosis under strong stratification, and a mixing coefficient remaining near 10^-1 with a modest peak near Kelvin–Helmholtz activity.
watch_item: The apparent upscale perpendicular flux should not be interpreted as a true inverse cascade, since it is attributed to anisotropic redistribution rather than net energy transfer to larger scales.
paper_title: Energy transfer, Intermittency and Mixing in Shear-Driven Stratified Turbulence
